claim_or_decision: M1 is admitted only against an exact GapDB source, module, binary digest, protocol, storage, platform, and filesystem tuple
observation: Admission pins ff3dd478, the pseudo-version and sums, sidecar SHA-256, protocol/storage v1, Linux/amd64, one host, local filesystem semantics, and two identical builds
decision_effect: Build into a project-owned directory, hash the configured absolute path, and reject PATH or @latest discovery
open_risk: No release tag exists

claim_or_decision: Human signature is an exit gate, not an experiment-entry prerequisite
observation: Admission names github:lynncoleart and requires a signature over the exact tested tuple/evidence at exit
decision_effect: Run machine qualification first; request signature only after every M1 technical gate passes
open_risk: A changed tuple invalidates the signature target and requires requalification

claim_or_decision: M1 must stop the program before M2 if the zombie scenario loses single authority or canonical digest equality
observation: The admission and program both declare a hard stop around the crown-jewel stale-writer/recovery claim
decision_effect: Encode the stop rule in acceptance evidence and do not downgrade it to a waiver
open_risk: A superficially passing adapter suite could conceal a product-authority failure

claim_or_decision: One accepted command is one durable GapDB batch containing events, operation result, heads, due checkpoint data, and effect intent
observation: Architecture orders canonicalization, idempotency, preconditions, pure reduction, one conditional durable batch, then publication and effect dispatch
decision_effect: Design a single AtomicBatch with AckDurable and conditional records; no split publication path
open_risk: Batch may exceed limits unless budgets are explicit

claim_or_decision: GapDB batch revisions cannot be embedded into values or keys in that same batch
observation: The server assigns the one global revision at acceptance, after the client has encoded all mutations
decision_effect: Use immutable preallocated EventIDs; derive replay order from Record.Revision plus event_index and EventID
open_risk: The adapter must preserve record metadata during scans and reconciliation

claim_or_decision: Operation replay is keyed by OperationID plus canonical request digest
observation: Same identity/digest returns the recorded typed outcome; a different digest is a conflict; lost durable responses are ambiguous
decision_effect: Insert the operation record with require-absent in the command batch and read-reconcile the same key before any retry effect
open_risk: A transport retry that invents a new OperationID would duplicate work

claim_or_decision: Only the durable batch can authorize live publication or external effect dispatch
observation: AckDurable covers WAL synchronization before response/publication, while AckMemory is only memory-visible
decision_effect: Use AckDurable for all authority commands and publish in-memory events only after success or read reconciliation
open_risk: An ambiguous response requires bounded reconciliation rather than assumed failure

claim_or_decision: Product events and reducers must be bounded and explicitly versioned
observation: Recovery is closed when journal integrity, event schema, or reducer compatibility cannot be established
decision_effect: Persist event schema/reducer versions and registry digests; reject unknown versions and oversized commands before publication
open_risk: Migration/compatibility policy beyond the admitted reducer set remains future work

claim_or_decision: Every restart creates a new durable runtime epoch before commands are admitted
observation: Recovery order requires byte recovery, product restore, a new epoch, predecessor lease invalidation/quarantine, effect reconciliation, then readiness
decision_effect: Keep an admission barrier closed through restore and create the epoch durably even after a clean shutdown
open_risk: Host crash during epoch transition needs an explicit recoverable operation

claim_or_decision: Checkpoint-plus-suffix replay has deterministic precedence and no force-ready override
observation: The runtime validates the full compatible journal, selects the newest valid checkpoint inside a revision-pinned budget, otherwise bounded full replay, otherwise degraded/refused
decision_effect: Store checkpoint prefix/version/state digests and test valid, corrupt, incompatible, and over-budget candidates
open_risk: The exact checkpoint cadence and product budget are undecided

claim_or_decision: Playback must be side-effect free and produce the same canonical digest as restored live state
observation: Playback uses fixed reducers and recorded observations and may not invoke Git, filesystem, tracker, qualification, artifacts, outbox, or compensation
decision_effect: Construct playback without adapter implementations and add panic/counting sentinels asserting exactly zero calls
open_risk: Noncanonical serialization or map iteration could cause false digest drift

claim_or_decision: A fencing token cannot prevent direct filesystem writes by a zombie
observation: Historical and architectural evidence requires immutable lease/workspace binding and fresh replacement workspaces
decision_effect: Permanently quarantine W1 when its lease expires; allocate W3 to the replacement; refuse W1 capsules at handoff/review/integration
open_risk: The zombie can still consume disk or write files; quarantine is authority isolation, not OS write prevention

claim_or_decision: The five M1 GapDB fault cuts are distinct from all historical evidence counts
observation: M1 names cuts before publication, after acceptance/before response, after workspace creation/before binding, after binding/before capsule response, and after effect intent/before observation
decision_effect: Implement and report five new cut outcomes with universal invariant checks
open_risk: Test hooks must cut the real external boundary rather than an in-process surrogate

claim_or_decision: The historical top-level-test count is 73
observation: Phase 3 qualification reports 73 of 73 top-level tests in the historical-full-scenario census
decision_effect: Label this count as historical top-level Go tests only
open_risk: Conflating it with scenario cases would overstate coverage

claim_or_decision: The Phase 1 behavioral catalog contains 35 cases
observation: The catalog enumerates P1-01..P1-28 and WR-01..WR-07, with 31 complete and four partial
decision_effect: Use the catalog as a behavior inventory, not as a passed-test total
open_risk: Four partial historical cases remain partial rather than silently complete

claim_or_decision: The Phase 1 campaign contains 28 named crash cuts
observation: The mission review identifies SR-00..09, HR-00..07, and IG-00..09
decision_effect: Preserve their invariant meanings and label them boundary/subtest cuts
open_risk: They were proven in the historical SQLite/helper composition

claim_or_decision: The frozen Phase 1 campaign exercises 17 top-level tests
observation: Seventeen discovered tests were partitioned into 65 disjoint shards and repeated 100 times
decision_effect: Keep 17 separate from the 28 crash-cut count
open_risk: Historical repetition does not prove the external GapDB boundary

claim_or_decision: Phase 3 adds nine supplemental transaction, saga, and post-commit boundaries
observation: Qualification evidence lists exactly nine MM-prefixed boundary IDs
decision_effect: Carry these as a separate Phase 3 evidence class and preserve their semantics
open_risk: Do not sum nine and 28 as equivalent units

claim_or_decision: Historical Phase 1 and Phase 3 evidence is a design input rather than M1 adoption evidence
observation: Those campaigns used SQLite and helper-based process composition
decision_effect: Port universal invariants and fault intent, then re-prove them at the external GapDB product boundary
open_risk: A broad historical pass can create false confidence if storage/lifecycle differences are ignored

claim_or_decision: Prior GapDB evidence passed 14 portable-adapter scenarios but did not approve adoption
observation: The record says 14 pass while technical gates are incomplete, production backend remains SQLite, and human approval is absent
decision_effect: Treat it as contract/design evidence only and re-run all 14 through external gapdbd
open_risk: The prior adapter used repository-internal composition

claim_or_decision: All 14 portable scenarios must execute through the public external daemon
observation: The contract covers get/put, conditionals, batch, scan, watch, expiry, memory/durable ack, inspect, four authority cases, and response-loss reconciliation
decision_effect: Build an M1 external adapter with real start/restart/socket/response cutting; report 14/14 IDs individually
open_risk: A convenience import of internal/server would invalidate the evidence

claim_or_decision: GapDB's default limits require stricter product budgets
observation: Defaults are 4-KiB keys, 8-MiB values, 16-MiB frames/batches, 1,024 batch operations, 1,000 scan records, and bounded watch/client history
decision_effect: Define lower key/value/checkpoint/batch/event-count budgets and reject over-budget commands before any mutation
open_risk: Realistic checkpoint size is not yet measured

claim_or_decision: Watch is a notification mechanism, not the durable recovery journal
observation: Watch buffers and retained history are bounded, while the journal must survive disconnect/overflow/restart
decision_effect: On watch loss rebuild from immutable journal records and projection heads
open_risk: The exact overflow/rebuild trigger needs adapter tests

claim_or_decision: GapDB byte recovery and Spec Kitty semantic recovery are separate stages
observation: GapDB recovers snapshot/WAL bytes and fails closed on storage-chain errors; Spec Kitty must validate journal/reducer/checkpoint semantics afterward
decision_effect: Expose distinct health/refusal evidence for storage recovery and product restore
open_risk: Operators need enough diagnostics without a force-ready escape

claim_or_decision: The daemon readiness message is insufficient to identify the admitted owner
observation: Readiness contains schema, ready, and socket path; status later contains database ID, owner PID/start, revisions, lifecycle, and limits but not executable digest/source
decision_effect: Hash configured executable pre-spawn, record process identity, require status+health/database binding before command admission
open_risk: No cryptographic binding joins pre-exec digest to a reconnecting orphan

claim_or_decision: Daemon lifecycle ownership is a host responsibility and must fail closed
observation: gapdbd stops on SIGINT/SIGTERM and exposes no shutdown RPC; admission forbids takeover of an unknown owner
decision_effect: Signal only a process the host started and still proves it owns; reconnect an orphan only after digest/socket/database/lock/process provenance
open_risk: PID reuse and incomplete self-identification may require an upstream GapDB enhancement

claim_or_decision: General @latest/PATH installation instructions do not override the admitted build recipe
observation: README usage is generic while the admission pins module version, toolchain, trimpath recipe, output path, and SHA
decision_effect: Qualification scripts must reject unpinned or path-discovered binaries
open_risk: Developers may accidentally run a different local gapdbd

claim_or_decision: Expiry mechanics do not transfer product workspace authority
observation: The portable contract proves an expired record can release a storage key; the product law permanently binds a workspace to its old lease
decision_effect: Record lease expiry as a product event, quarantine the workspace, and create a fresh binding for the replacement
open_risk: Treating TTL absence as sufficient authority would recreate the stale-writer bug

claim_or_decision: External-effect recovery must compare before repeat or compensation
observation: Attribution-safe compensation requires provider revision, value, and operation marker still match the intent
decision_effect: Persist stable intent/attempt/observation identities and test a slow, unavailable, stale, and human-modified provider
open_risk: Provider APIs may not expose all attribution fields; unsupported cases must require operator action

claim_or_decision: The recommended plan is a sequence of executable evidence slices rather than package scaffolding
observation: The hardest architectural claim couples external durability, process lifetime, filesystem state, Git state, and authority
decision_effect: Deliver sidecar qualification, one-batch journal, restore/playback, workspace quarantine, effect reconciliation, then the full torture chamber
open_risk: Parallel scaffolding could obscure whether the crown-jewel scenario actually works

claim_or_decision: The external adapter may not parse human-formatted CLI output
observation: The admitted contract is the typed protocol-v1 Unix-socket surface
decision_effect: Consume typed public client status, health, and command results only
open_risk: Daemon startup readiness JSON still needs bounded parsing and provenance correlation

claim_or_decision: A global runtime-epoch guard need not be rewritten in every command batch in the single-owner M1 model
observation: GapDB has conditional mutations but no check-only batch predicate; touching one global epoch key would serialize independent aggregate commands
decision_effect: Use the host admission barrier plus epoch-pinned conditional aggregate/lease heads; forbid direct client access to GapDB
open_risk: This reasoning relies on one owning host and must be revisited before any multi-host design

claim_or_decision: Journal compaction is outside M1
observation: M1 is a narrow proving slice centered on recovery correctness rather than retention policy
decision_effect: Retain immutable journal/checkpoint records for the entire evidence run
open_risk: Long-running capacity and safe compaction remain later milestones

claim_or_decision: Public scan cursors pin the observed revision and fail stale rather than mixing revisions
observation: ScanPage exposes ObservedRevision and Cursor; a database change between pages produces SCAN_STALE and restart-scan guidance
decision_effect: Traverse all journal pages with command admission closed, assert one observed revision, and restart the whole scan on stale
open_risk: M1 still must prove this behavior through external gapdbd rather than only source inspection
